newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada posts ex-Europe cargo space on internet.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada posts ex-Europe cargo space on internet.

text.p: Air Canada has begun posting advisories on its Internet site listing last minute cargo space availability for the airline's North Atlantic system.

The advisories, posted each Thursday for the week following, (beginning Mondays) were inaugurated two weeks ago, says Gerry Simpson, cargo marketing manager, adding that he is unaware of any other airline providing flight-specific availability via the Internet.
The initial advisories list only flights from Europe to Canada; other corridors will be added soon, he told Reuters.
For example, "Toronto to London on a Monday is a day we have a lot of frequencies, and that's the kind of opportunity that should be added to the list."
For now, customers can only book space off the Internet list by telephoning Air Canada, said Simpson.

The space availability advisory for June 23-29 lists 43 departures on 14 routes from three European gateways: Frankfurt, London and Paris. This represents about 40 percent of the flights from those gateways.
Each listing includes flight times, aircraft type and days where space is available, but no details such as how many pallet positions are open and no rate information.
Simpson said the decision to list a flight is arbitrary. Most non-listed flights have little or no uncommitted space to offer.
Not listed for the June 23-29 advisory were any Zurich departures, any Paris-Montreal or Frankfurt-Calgary flights. Only five of 19 Frankfurt departures were listed.
Space was available daily from London to both Vancouver and Calgary.
Simpson said the large number of non-listed flights reflects the strength of market conditions so far this summer.
"Quite frankly, most of our flights are quite full; you're talking very high weight and space load factors," he said.

The list is aimed at all customers. Knowing about recurring opportunities could help a large forwarder persuade a customer to adjust shipping patterns, moving goods earlier in the week to avoid bottlenecks on particular corridors, he said.
There has been a steady growth in customer interest in Air Canada Cargo's Internet services, said Simpson.

Automated tracking and tracing of shipments was inaugurated in August 1996. Customer-initiated traces have grown from 41 in the first month and 115 in September to over 2,500 a month today, said Simpson.
Air Canada's Internet address is http://www.aircanada.ca -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
